# H1 diagnostic source catalogue

Historical main inventory at `b8816902`. Retired paths are text rather than live links; see the [native merge mapping](goway-merge-main-h1-port.md).

This is the historical Review 7 construction inventory. Review 8 corrections and
current acceptance are tracked in [the containment evidence](main-h1-error-containment.md#review-8-corrections-current-worktree).
The lexical inventory is not a proof of whole-pipeline containment.


This catalogue lists the diagnostic construction sites captured by the [Review 7 source inventory](main-h1-error-containment.md#review-7-correction-scope). It retains exact source locations and construction expressions for handwritten runtime, generated runtime, and developer tooling.

An arbitrary callback can return any diagnostic in this global catalogue. Local family links in the boundary table identify source packages for navigation. They do not restrict or establish transitive reachability. The shared source-marker contract applies universally, while dedicated public-path regressions establish individual source pipelines. A lexical construction or boundary row is not a separate integration-test claim.

Construction and containment are separate roles. `WrapFault`, `WrapFailure`, `Owned`, and `Prefix` rows also appear in the main boundary inventory, including snapshots or wrappers around non-nil causes. Counts across those indexes overlap. Message-forwarding factory callsites include their caller-supplied source expressions. Factory discovery follows free functions returning error whose message string parameter reaches a known constructor or another discovered factory. Enum-parameter error factories are additional source candidates. Their public or conditional ownership contracts remain distinct from trusted owner snapshots. Factory names do not establish trusted provenance. Typed literals and formatted errors are review candidates. They do not gain trusted provenance merely by appearing in this index. Public application-created faults, storage failures, and database NewError values do not acquire diagnostic provenance. The private database owner separately snapshots its known operations and codes after outcome mutation. Tooling entries describe CLI, compiler, generator, and release diagnostics outside the runtime boundary claim.

The current full verification and required PostgreSQL gates passed; execution results are recorded in the companion containment evidence. This catalogue is a source inventory, not an independent test run.

## Direct named-error enum emissions

These are raw named-error values emitted in an error return position or assigned to an explicit error variable. They do not acquire ownership from their Error method or enum type. Entries include intentional public/custom fallbacks and control values, and are review candidates rather than automatically confirmed containment gaps. Code-valued classification data returns are excluded.

| Source | Owner | Emission kind | Expression and resolved type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [websocket/code_diagnostics.go:15](../../websocket/code_diagnostics.go) | codeFailure | direct named-error enum return | `code / type websocket.Code / runtime` |

The remaining direct emission is the default branch of private WebSocket codeFailure. Its sixteen known protocol constants use the owned branch. The default returns an unknown or application-supplied Code without granting ownership, so containment keeps generic redaction. It is not an unmarked built-in constant source.
